text.text: A ten-minute tour of the driving school in this workspace. Share it with the owner, every instructor and the office.
: each learner's package, permit date, age, classroom hours, behind-the-wheel hours, parent log hours, road test requirements and attempts.

: theory classes with topic, instructor, seats and attendance.

: every attempt, with the site, coach, points lost and the examiner's notes.
Monday: lessons for the week confirmed; cars checked against bookings.
Every day: instructors mark lessons and write the next skills.
Wednesday: learners whose requirements are met get a road test booked.
Friday: the owner reads the Dashboard: learners by stage, tests coming up, cars due for service.
Every morning: today's lessons and the pre-drive car check
Every week: classroom attendance entered, parent logs updated
Every month: car service and inspection dates, no-shows followed up
Every quarter: road test pass rate by instructor
The owner runs bookings, cars and the classroom calendar. Instructors own lessons, notes and test readiness. Parents of learners under 18 own the practice log.

Packages are paid before the first drive, or half up front and half before the road test. Lessons cancelled with less than 24 hours' notice are counted as used, and the office tells the family the same day.
Learners under 18 appear by first name and last initial. Permit numbers and parents' phone numbers stay in the learner's file, not in notes.

Rename packages, focuses and test sites, change the road test formula to your state's rule, and delete the sample rows once your own are in. Edit any cell in place; hours and requirements update by themselves.

text.text: Who is ready for a road test
A new driver's first hour sets the tone for everything after. Calm, quiet streets and clear words build confidence; a busy road on day one can scare someone off driving for months.
date and see the permit in person. No permit, no drive.
For learners under 18, a parent signs the enrollment form and gets the parent practice log.
Read any notes from the classroom instructor.
Book the car and route in
Adjust seat, mirrors, headrest and steering wheel
Seat belt, doors locked, phone off and out of reach
Hands at nine and three; feet on the right pedals
Start, stop and steer at walking speed
Pulling away and stopping smoothly at the curb.
Right turns, then left turns, at quiet corners.
Stop signs: full stop, look left, right, left.
Use the dual brake only when needed, and explain why afterward without blame.
Park, turn off the engine, and talk: two things that went well, one to practice. Write them in
Parents are part of the training. Tell them what to practice and where. A good parent drive is twenty to thirty minutes on familiar streets, several times a week. The learner logs every drive in the
Go slower than you planned. Stay in the lot for the whole hour if needed. Confidence comes from small wins.

Delphine, fifteen, has had her permit ten days. Her instructor spends twenty minutes in the lot and thirty on quiet streets near the school. She stops smoothly by the end. The note for next time says: left turns and checking mirrors before pulling away; her parent is asked to practice in the lot on Sunday.
Most road test failures come from a few habits: rolling stops, not checking blind spots, and nerves. Practice the test, not just driving, and learners pass the first time.

Gustavo is booked in six days. His record shows 30 classroom hours, 7 behind the wheel and 61 logged with his parent, so requirements are met. Two test-practice lessons on the east route focus on full stops and blind spots. He passes with six points lost.
A training car carries a new driver and an instructor every hour of the day. It must be safe, legal and clean every time it leaves the lot.
Walk around: tires, lights, signals, mirrors, dents
Dual-control brake tested at walking speed
Learner signs and the "student driver" magnet in place
. Book service a week ahead so the car is never out on a busy afternoon. When a car is in the shop, set it to
so nobody books it, and move its lessons to another car.
The instructor's brake is the most important part of the car. Have it checked at every service and after any hard stop. If it feels soft or spongy, the car stops being used until it is repaired.
Any bump, however small, is written up the same day: date, place, what happened, photos, and who was driving. Tell the owner the same day and the insurer within their deadline.

Learners notice a dirty car and judge the school by it. Empty the car after every lesson, wipe the wheel and gear stick at the end of each day, and keep a box of tissues and hand gel in the glove box.
Training cars work hard. Plan to replace each one at around 120,000 miles or when repairs in a year cost more than a third of its value.
